We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 5 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <= $9999. We have no price data, but assume typical small molecules are cheap. Need to construct route using templates.

Target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

Looks like a polyunsaturated fatty acid derivative with a cyclic diol (maybe a protected sugar?). Actually it's a cyclohexane with two hydroxyls and an ether linking to a polyene chain ending with carboxylic acid.

Simplify: It's a cyclic diol (maybe a cyclohexane) with an O-alkyl side chain: O-CH (attached to cyclohexane) linking to a polyene chain with terminal COOH and a side CH2OH? Wait: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

Interpret: Cyclohexane ring with two OH groups (one free, one as ether). The ether attaches to a side chain: O-CH (attached to ring) then CH (attached to side chain) with a double bond to C(CO)/C (i.e., a vinyl with CH2OH). Then chain continues with conjugated double bonds to a carboxylic acid.

Potential disconnections:
- Break the ether bond: O-alkyl cleavage to give a diol cyclohexanol and an allylic alcohol (or aldehyde). Use template 37276 which gave two possible precursors: C/C(=C/[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)CC=C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)CO and C/C(=C/[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)C=CC/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)CO. Those are similar but not exactly the target? Actually the template seems to break an ether to give an alcohol and a carbonyl? Not sure.

We could consider a simpler route: start from commercially available cyclohexane-1,2-diol (cis? maybe). And a polyene acid like (E,E,E)-heptatrienoic acid? The side chain: C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O is a conjugated triene acid (maybe (E,E)-penta-2,4-dienoic acid?). Actually chain length: after the ether O, there is a carbon attached to the ring (C*), then /C=C/ (double bond) then /C=C/ then /C=C/ then C(O)=O. That's a 4 double bond chain (but one is attached to CH2OH). The side chain also has a CH2OH at the first double bond (C=C(CO)/C). So it's a 3 double bond chain with a terminal COOH and a side CH2OH.

Potential building block: (E)-3-hydroxy-2-methyl-2-butenyl? Might be complex.

Given limited time, maybe propose a route using known reactions: 1) Start from cyclohexane-1,2-diol (commercial). 2) Protect one OH as TBDMS (protecting group). 3) Perform O-alkylation with an allylic bromide (e.g., 3-bromo-2-methyl-2-propen-1-ol) to form ether. 4) Deprotect TBDMS. 5) Oxidize terminal alkene to carboxylic acid via ozonolysis or oxidative cleavage (but that would break double bonds). Might need to build polyene via Wittig or cross-coupling.

Alternative: Use a polyene acid (e.g., (E,E)-hexa-2,4-dienoic acid) and couple via esterification to the diol? Not.

Given constraints, maybe propose a route using known building blocks: (i) Cyclohexane-1,2-diol (SMILES O[C@H]1CCCC[C@@H]1O) is buyable. (ii) 3-bromo-2-methyl-2-propen-1-ol (SMILES C=C(CO)CBr) maybe buyable? Check is_buyable.
